subject: Follow-up: DPA details — dataflow, subprocessors, breach notification timing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan@medsync.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA items & dataflow summary

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for a constructive demo this morning. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on for your legal/ops review:

- Attachments included: Redwood-DPA_v1.3.pdf (our proposed addendum), dataflow_diagram.png (how MedSync data traverses Redwood runtime), subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (current subprocessor list).
- Specific asks from your team: clarification on controller vs processor responsibilities for PII we will process, retention windows for logs and embeddings, breach notification SLA and the subprocessor notification flow.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll answer the three core questions below in writing and mark proposed DPA text edits for each point.
2) If helpful, our legal team can prepare a short one-page summary mapping responsibilities for your SI/Legal Ops.
3) Can we set a follow-up on Mon 7/19 at 10am PT to review redlines live?

Questions to confirm from your side: are there any additional internal approvers beyond Legal Ops (copied) and the product/security stakeholders?

Thanks — I’m looping Monica who will coordinate evidence and Ben who will pull logs for the sample retention proof.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-DPA_v1.3.pdf (27KB, pdf), dataflow_diagram.png (120KB, png), subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (15KB, xlsx)

From: Evan Morris <evan@medsync.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medsync.com>, Claire Zhang <claire@healthsyncpartners.io>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA items & dataflow summary

Karthik —

Thanks for the notes and the materials. A few clarifying questions after a quick pass through the DPA draft:

1) Controller vs Processor: we need explicit language that MedSync is the controller for patient-identifiable data and Redwood is the processor. In particular, who is responsible for logging and storing request metadata (IP, request timestamp, request body snippets) for debugging/abuse purposes? We need to ensure logs with potential PII are retained/stored according to our retention policy.

2) Retention windows: can you confirm default retention for (a) inference logs (request/response snippets), (b) full embeddings derived from customer data, and (c) KV cache artifacts? We will likely require a 90-day maximum for inference logs and a 180-day maximum for embeddings unless we can get a contractual guarantee around deletion on demand.

3) Subprocessors: the matrix looks comprehensive but can you provide a short mapping that ties each subprocessor to the data flow stage (e.g., model hosting, observability/logging, metrics/analytics)? We need to present a subprocessor mapping to our vendor-risk team.

4) Breach notification: your DPA mentions "prompt" notification — we need a narrower window. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to notification within 48 hours of confirming a security incident that affects MedSync data? Also, what is the escalation path (who is notified internally at Redwood)?

If you can respond in writing before our Legal Ops sync tomorrow afternoon, that would be ideal.

—Evan
Evan Morris
Head of Product, MedSync Health

Attachment referenced: MedSync_DPA_comments_20280718.docx (we’ve added inline redlines)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: answers for MedSync questions (draft)

Karthik / Ben —

Draft answers to Evan’s questions for review before we send externally. I’m summarizing and attaching a one-page evidence bundle we can share if Legal signs off.

1) Controller vs Processor / Logging: Redwood operates as the processor for customer-provided content. Operational logs are collected by our observability pipeline (hosted in Redwood-managed accounts for Hosted customers). We can provide three options in the DPA:
   - Option A (default hosted): Redwood retains operational logs containing request metadata for 90 days. Logs may include request timestamps, IPs (anonymized on request), and up to 256 bytes of request snippet for debugging.
   - Option B (privacy-tight): Redwood retains only anonymized telemetry for 30 days and redacts request snippets; customers must enable an opt-in evidence package for longer retention.
   - Option C (dedicated/private): For Dedicated/Private deployments we can adopt customer-controlled logging (logs land in customer-owned buckets) and align to your retention policy.

2) Retention windows: embeddings are retained by default for 180 days; we can add contractual deletion-on-demand within 5 business days for customer-marked content. KV cache persists for the session scope (ephemeral) unless configured for longer; we can propose a max-ttl clause.

3) Subprocessors mapping: attached subprocessor_matrix.xlsx includes columns we can populate: name / function / country / data stage. I’ll populate the mapping for the three highest-risk subprocessors (model hosting, metrics/analytics, logging) and highlight EU-hosted options.

4) Breach notification: Legal recommends "as soon as reasonably practicable and within 72 hours of confirmation" as a starting point. For customers requiring 48 hours, we can escalate to a formal SLA amendment with our Incident Response team and a named point-of-contact. Internal escalation path: Security Ops -> Product Security Lead (Ben Carter) -> Head of Legal (copy).

Attachments I plan to share with the customer (pending Karthik/Ben sign-off): evidence_sample.log (redacted), one_page_dpa_mapping.pdf

Can you both review and flag any edits? I’ll update the DPA redline comments as we agree.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_sample.log (1.2KB, txt), one_page_dpa_mapping.pdf (12KB, pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan@medsync.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medsync.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA items & dataflow summary

Evan —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are our commitments and a proposed next step (DocuSign) if this aligns with MedSync needs. I’ve also attached the one-page mapping we discussed and a short excerpt of DPA text with the suggested edit highlights.

1) Controller/Processor & Logging: Confirmed — MedSync is Controller; Redwood is Processor. For Hosted customers (default):
   - Operational logs: 90-day retention (can anonymize IP on request). Request snippets are limited to 256 bytes and stored encrypted.
   - Option for Dedicated/Private: logs can be routed to customer-owned storage and retention fully controlled by MedSync.

2) Retention:
   - Inference logs (request/response snippets): 90 days by default, deletion-on-demand within 5 business days after request.
   - Embeddings: 180 days by default, or deletion-on-demand within 5 business days if flagged in writing.
   - KV cache: ephemeral by session; configurable TTL for longer sessions (we can add a max-ttl clause).

3) Subprocessors mapping: attached matrix now shows primary subprocessor roles (hosting, model ops, logging/observability, analytics) and the dataflow stage each supports. We will provide a separate CSV for your vendor-risk team with country and SOC/Tier info.

4) Breach notification: Redwood commits to notification to MedSync (Legal Ops) within 72 hours of incident confirmation for standard contracts. If MedSync requires a 48-hour contractual timeline, we can accept that with an ISR (Incident SLA Rider) and a named escalation point (Ben Carter as Product Security Lead, and Monica as Customer Solutions lead).

If this looks good I’ll: (a) upload the redline DPA to DocuSign for MedSync Legal to review, and (b) schedule the 7/19 10am PT working session if that still works for your stakeholders.

Proposed DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/home/documents/0a1b2c3d
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Shall I proceed to send the DocuSign envelope?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
